indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: BI.2.1.3: Show understanding of the roles of condensation, evaporation, transpiration and precipitation in the hydrological cycle
indicator.objective: Observe the disappearance of mist and pools of water after rains

skills.description: Observe and describe what happens to mist or a pool of water after rain
Predict what will happen to water left in the sun or shade

misconceptions: The water just vanishes into nothing.
Water only disappears when it is hot.
Puddles go into the ground only and never into the air.

questions.stem: After it rains, puddles of water form on the ground. Later, what happens to the puddles?
questions.explanation: Puddles disappear after some time because the water dries up.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the water stays forever.

options: Small drops of water in the air
hints: It looks like a cloud near the ground.
questions.explanation: Mist is made of tiny drops of water in the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think mist is smoke.

questions.stem: When a puddle of water dries up, where does the water go?
options: Into the sky as a cloud
Both into the ground and into the air
hints: Some goes up into the air.
questions.explanation: Puddle water can soak into the ground or evaporate into the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the water just vanishes.

questions.stem: What happens to wet clothes when you hang them in the sun?
questions.explanation: Wet clothes dry in the sun because the water evaporates (goes into the air).
questions.misconception: Pupils may think clothes only dry when it is windy.

questions.stem: If you leave a cup of water in the sun for a long time, what will happen?
options: The water will turn into juice
hints: The water goes into the air.
questions.explanation: The water will decrease because it evaporates into the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the water level stays the same.

questions.stem: Kofi sees mist early in the morning. A few hours later, the mist is gone. What happened to the mist?
questions.explanation: The mist disappeared into the air (it evaporated).
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the mist turned into something else.

questions.stem: Where does water from a drying puddle go?
hints: It goes into the air or ground.
questions.explanation: The water goes into the air (evaporation) or into the ground.

questions.stem: Why do puddles dry up faster on a sunny day than on a cloudy day?
options: Because the sun helps the water evaporate faster
Because it rains on sunny days
Because the wind blows the puddles away
questions.explanation: The sun provides heat, which helps water evaporate faster.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the sun directly 'drinks' the water.

questions.stem: What is the process called when water turns into gas and goes into the air?
hints: It happens when puddles dry up.
questions.explanation: Evaporation is when water turns into gas and goes into the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse evaporation with boiling.

questions.stem: If you put two identical puddles of water, one in the sun and one in the shade, which will dry up first?
options: Both will dry at the same time
questions.explanation: The puddle in the sun will dry up first because the heat from the sun helps water evaporate faster.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think shade helps water dry.

questions.stem: What happens to wet clothes when you hang them outside on a sunny day?
hints: The water goes into the air.
questions.explanation: Wet clothes dry when hung in the sun because the water evaporates.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the clothes stay wet until it rains.

questions.stem: Ama leaves a glass of water outside for two days. The water level goes down. Why?
options: The water evaporated into the air
The water turned into a solid
questions.explanation: The water evaporated into the air because of the heat.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the glass absorbed the water.

questions.stem: You see a puddle of water on the ground in the morning. What do you predict it will look like in the afternoon? Explain why.

criteria.description: States the puddle will be smaller or gone
Explains that the water evaporates into the air

questions.explanation: The puddle will get smaller or disappear because the sun helps the water evaporate.

questions.stem: Put a little water on two plates. Put one plate in the sun and one in the shade. Check them after an hour. Tell your teacher what you observed.

criteria.description: Observes and states that the plate in the sun dried faster
States that the heat from the sun helps water disappear

hints: Does heat make water dry faster?
questions.explanation: The plate in the sun will dry faster because heat from the sun helps the water evaporate.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a way water disappears from the ground?
hints: Think about what actually happens to puddles.
questions.explanation: Water does not turn into stone. It evaporates or soaks into the ground.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not understand the limits of transformation.

questions.stem: What causes mist to disappear after the sun comes out?
options: The mist is blown away by the wind
The tiny water drops in the mist evaporate into the air
The mist falls to the ground as rain
hints: The tiny water drops dry up.
questions.explanation: The tiny water drops in the mist evaporate into the air when the sun heats them.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the mist is always blown away by the wind.

questions.stem: Why is it easier to dry clothes on a windy, sunny day than on a still, cloudy day?
options: The wind blows the water away
The wind and sun help the water evaporate faster
The sun makes the clothes heavier
The wind makes the clothes dry faster
questions.explanation: Both wind and sun help water evaporate faster, so clothes dry more quickly.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the wind physically 'blows' the water off, which is partly true but evaporation is the main process.

questions.stem: A student puts a small puddle of water in the freezer. What will happen to the water?
hints: Water freezes when it gets cold.
questions.explanation: The water will freeze and turn into ice because the freezer is very cold.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think water always evaporates regardless of temperature.

questions.stem: Write two places where puddle water goes when it dries up.

criteria.description: States it goes into the air (evaporates)
States it goes into the ground

questions.explanation: The water goes into the air (evaporation) and into the ground.
